title: Design System: FSSC AP Training Guide

display.purpose: Page titles only (h1.page-title). One per page.

body.purpose: All prose: descriptions, step text, definitions, card copy.

label.purpose: Every non-prose string: nav captions, tags, codes, category titles, glossary headwords, region badges.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The floating search-results dropdown. Only UI-chrome shadow in the system.

shadows.name: embedded-media
shadows.purpose: Step screenshots (.wi-step-img) — a light lift off the surrounding card.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Background/border-color transitions on hover, theme switch, and focus. No transform/scale motion anywhere in the system.

components.name: Nav Item
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: 9px 12px; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; color: var(--ink-soft); font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--surface-alt); color: var(--ink); } .ds-nav-icon { width: 16px; text-align: center; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 12px; }

components.name: Nav Item — Active
components.css: .ds-nav-item-active { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; padding: 9px 12px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--blue-soft); color: var(--blue); font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; }

components.name: Tag
components.description: Keyword chip used on case/WI cards.
components.css: .ds-tag { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 10.5px; background: var(--surface-alt); color: var(--ink-soft); padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 20px; display: inline-block; }

components.name: Card
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: 20px 22px; }

components.name: Search Input
components.description: Topbar search field with inline icon.
components.html: ⌕
components.css: .ds-search-wrap { position: relative; } .ds-search-input { width: 100%; padding: 10px 14px 10px 38px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; font-size: 14px; background: var(--surface-alt); color: var(--ink); outline: none; transition: border-color .15s, background .15s; } .ds-search-input:focus { border-color: var(--blue); background: #fff; } .ds-search-icon { position: absolute; left: 12px; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); color: var(--ink-faint); font-size: 14px; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Flow Node — Linked
components.description: Signature component: a clickable process-diagram step wired to a specific Work Instruction step.
components.html: Revisar encabezado y líneaswi-3way-match-ca · step 9
components.css: .ds-flow-node { background: var(--surface); border: 1.5px solid var(--blue); border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px 20px; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; text-align: center; min-width: 220px; display: inline-block; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink); cursor: pointer; } .ds-flow-node:hover { background: var(--blue-soft); } .ds-flow-node-code { display: block; font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 10px; color: var(--ink-faint); font-weight: 400; margin-top: 3px; }

components.name: Flow Node — Pending
components.description: Non-clickable state for a diagram step with no content yet for the active region — the system's only dashed-border usage.
components.html: Enviar a HandoverContenido en construcción
components.css: .ds-flow-node-pending { border-style: dashed; border-color: var(--ink-faint); color: var(--ink-faint); cursor: default; }

narrative.overview:
This is a technical field manual, not a marketing surface: a reference a new SGS Accounts Payable hire keeps open next to Oracle while they work, built to be scanned under pressure rather than admired. The system is precise and quietly confident — it earns trust through consistency and restraint, not through decoration. Every visual decision optimizes for one question: can someone who has never seen this screen before find the exact step they need in seconds?

The palette stays cool and procedural (Ledger Blue, Verification Teal, Confirmed Green, Flagged Amber) with a near-total absence of ornament: no illustration, no gradients beyond a single small brand mark, no shadows except where content genuinely floats above the page. Monospace type is used deliberately and everywhere status matters — tags, captions, region codes, step counters — so machine-like, verifiable information reads as distinct from prose the instant your eye lands on it.
keyCharacteristics: Cool, restrained four-color semantic palette (blue/teal/green/amber), each color owning one meaning and never used decoratively
Monospace for every label, tag, code, and status string; humanist sans for everything a person reads as prose
Flat by default — 1px borders delineate surfaces; shadows appear only on floating/overlay content
Numbered, connected steps (a literal spine with counter badges) as the primary content pattern, not paragraphs

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Blue means interactive, teal means informational/decision, green means completion/category, amber means incomplete/caution. A color never borrows another color's meaning to fill a gap in the palette.

rules.name: The Label-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Any string that names a status, category, code, or system value renders in the Label treatment (monospace, uppercase, tracked), never as smaller Body text.

rules.name: The Flat-Unless-Floating Rule
rules.body: A shadow appears only when content overlaps something else in the same view (a dropdown over content, an image embedded in a step). Everything else sits flush and is separated by border alone.

dos: Do put any status, code, category, or tag in the Label treatment (monospace, uppercase, tracked) — never render it as small Body text.
Do use a dashed border exclusively to mean "not yet available." Never use it for decoration or a different kind of emphasis.
Do keep shadows reserved for content that visually floats over other content (dropdowns, embedded images). A card sitting in normal flow never gets a shadow.

Do let a color's assigned meaning constrain its use: Ledger Blue for interactive/navigational, Verification Teal for informational/decision, Confirmed Green for completion/category, Flagged Amber for caution/incomplete.
donts: Don't introduce a generic filled "primary button" component — this system routes every action through a card, a flow node, or a toggle segment instead.
Don't add illustration, photography, or gradients beyond the existing small two-color brand mark. The system is text- and structure-led.
Don't use Confirmed Green or Flagged Amber for navigation or emphasis outside their assigned meaning.
